paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 26 to 35 are based on the following passage.
paragraphs.translationZh: 第 26 至 35 题基于以下段落。

paragraphs.sourceText: Just off the coast of Southern California sits Santa Cruz Island, where a magical creature called the island fox 26 . A decade ago, this island’s ecosystem was in 27 . Wild pigs attracted golden eagles from the mainland, and those flying 28 crashed the fox population. So the Nature Conservancy launched a 29 war against the pigs, complete with helicopters and sharp shooters.
paragraphs.translationZh: 圣克鲁斯岛位于南加州海岸附近，岛上栖息着一种叫做岛狐的神奇生物。十年前，这座岛屿的生态系统一片混乱。野猪吸引了来自大陆的金雕，而那些飞行的掠食者则摧毁了狐狸的数量。于是，大自然保护协会对猪发动了一场激烈的战争，出动了直升机和神枪手。

paragraphs.sourceText: And it worked. Today, federal agencies are pulling the island fox from the Endangered Species List. It’s the fastest-ever recovery of a mammal, joining peers like the Louisiana black bear as glowing successes in the history of the Endangered Species Act.
paragraphs.translationZh: 它奏效了。今天，联邦机构正在将岛狐从濒危物种名单中删除。这是有史以来恢复最快的哺乳动物，与路易斯安那黑熊等同类一起成为《濒危物种法案》历史上的辉煌成功。

paragraphs.sourceText: But the recovery of Santa Cruz Island isn’t just about the fox. The Nature Conservancy has 30 war on a multitude of invasive species here, from sheep to plants to the 31 Argentine ant. “Our philosophy with the island has always been, ‘OK, 32 the threats and let the island go back to what it was,’” says ecologist Christina Boser. And it appears to be working. Native plants are coming back, and the fox once again bounds about carefree.
paragraphs.translationZh: 但圣克鲁斯岛的恢复不仅仅是狐狸的功劳。大自然保护协会已向这里的多种入侵物种宣战，从绵羊到植物，再到侵略性的阿根廷蚂蚁。 “我们对这座岛屿的理念一直是，‘好吧，消除威胁，让岛屿恢复到原来的样子，’”生态学家克里斯蒂娜·博瑟说。它似乎正在发挥作用。原生植物正在回归，狐狸又再次无忧无虑地蹦蹦跳跳。

paragraphs.sourceText: But keeping those foxes from harm will occupy Boser and her colleagues for years to come. You see, humans are still allowed on Santa Cruz Island, and they bring dogs. So Boser has to vaccinate her foxes against various diseases. “We’re obligated to keep a pulse on the population for at least five years after the foxes are delisted,” says Boser. That includes tagging the foxes and 33 their numbers to ensure nothing goes wrong.
paragraphs.translationZh: 但保护这些狐狸免受伤害将是博瑟和她的同事们未来几年的任务。你看，圣克鲁斯岛仍然允许人类进入，而且他们还带着狗。因此博瑟必须给她的狐狸接种各种疾病的疫苗。 “在狐狸被除名后，我们有义务至少在五年内对狐狸数量进行监测，”博泽说。这包括给狐狸贴上标签并监控它们的数量，以确保不会出现任何问题。

paragraphs.sourceText: This is the story of the little fox that has come back, and the people who have 34 their lives to protecting it. This is the story of wildlife conservation in the age of mass 35 .
paragraphs.translationZh: 这是回来的小狐狸和那些为保护它而献出生命的人们的故事。这是大灭绝时代野生动物保护的故事。

paragraphs.sourceText: Directions: In this section, you are going to read a passage with ten statements attached to it. Each statement contains information given in one of the paragraphs. Identify the paragraph from which the information is derived. You may choose a paragraph more than once. Each paragraph is marked with a letter. Answer the questions by marking the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 2.
paragraphs.translationZh: 说明：在本节中，您将阅读一段附有十个陈述的段落。每条陈述都包含其中一个段落中给出的信息。确定信息来源的段落。您可以多次选择一个段落。每个段落都标有一个字母。通过在答题卡 2 上标记相应的字母来回答问题。

paragraphs.sourceText: Do Parents Invade Children’s Privacy When They Post Photos Online?
paragraphs.translationZh: 父母在网上发布照片是否侵犯了孩子的隐私？

paragraphs.sourceText: A. When Katlyn Burbidge’s son was 6 years old, he was performing some ridiculous song and dance typical of a first-grader. But after she snapped a photo and started using her phone, he asked her a serious question:“Are you going to post that online?” She laughed and answered, “Yes, I think I will.” What he said next stopped her. “Can you not?”
paragraphs.translationZh: 答：当 Katlyn Burbidge 的儿子 6 岁时，他正在表演一些一年级学生典型的可笑的歌曲和舞蹈。但在她拍完照片并开始使用手机后，他问了她一个严肃的问题：“你要把它发布到网上吗？”她笑着回答：“是的，我想我会的。”他接下来的话让她停住了。 “你可以不吗？”

paragraphs.sourceText: B. That’s when it dawned on her: She had been posting photos of him online without asking his permission. “We’re big advocates of bodily autonomy and not forcing him to hug or kiss people unless he wants to, but it never occurred to me that I should ask his permission to post photos of him online,” says Burbidge, a mom of two in Wakefield, Massachusetts. “Now when I post a photo of him online, I show him the photo and get his okay.”
paragraphs.translationZh: B. 这时她才恍然大悟：她在未经他许可的情况下在网上发布了他的照片。 “我们是身体自主权的大力倡导者，除非他愿意，否则不会强迫他拥抱或亲吻别人，但我从来没有想过应该征求他的许可在网上发布他的照片，”马萨诸塞州韦克菲尔德的两个孩子的母亲伯比奇说。 “现在，当我在网上发布他的照片时，我会给他看照片并得到他的同意。”

paragraphs.sourceText: C. When her 8-month-old is 3 or 4 years old, she plans to start asking him in an age-appropriate way, “Do you want other people to see this?” That’s precisely the approach that two researchers advocated before a room of pediatricians (儿科医生) last week at the American Academy of Pediatrics meeting, when they discussed the 21st century challenge of “sharenting,” a new term for parents’ online sharing about their children. “As advocates of children’s rights, we believe that children should have a voice about what information is shared about them if possible,” says Stacey Steinberg, a legal skills professor at the University of Florida Levin College of Law in Gainesville.
paragraphs.translationZh: C. 当她 8 个月的孩子长到 3 或 4 岁时，她计划开始以适合年龄的方式问他：“你想让其他人看到这个吗？”这正是上周在美国儿科学会会议上，两位研究人员在儿科医生面前提倡的方法，当时他们讨论了“分享”这一 21 世纪的挑战，“分享”是父母在线分享孩子信息的新术语。盖恩斯维尔佛罗里达大学莱文法学院法律技能教授史黛西·斯坦伯格 (Stacey Steinberg) 表示：“作为儿童权利的倡导者，我们认为，如果可能的话，儿童应该对哪些有关他们的信息被分享有发言权。”

paragraphs.sourceText: D. Whether it’s ensuring that your child isn’t bullied over something you post, that their identity isn’t digitally “kidnapped”, or that their photos don’t end up on a half dozen child pornography (色情) sites, as one Australian mom discovered, parents and pediatricians are increasingly aware of the importance of protecting children’s digital presence. Steinberg and Bahareh Keith, an assistant professor of pediatrics at the University of Florida College of Medicine, say most children will likely never experience problems related to what their parents share, but a tension still exists between parents’ rights to share their experiences and their children’s rights to privacy.
paragraphs.translationZh: D. 正如一位澳大利亚妈妈发现的那样，无论是确保您的孩子不会因为您发布的内容而受到欺凌，还是确保他们的身份不会被数字化“绑架”，或者确保他们的照片不会出现在六个儿童色情网站上，家长和儿科医生都越来越意识到保护儿童数字存在的重要性。斯坦伯格和佛罗里达大学医学院儿科助理教授巴哈雷·基思表示，大多数孩子可能永远不会遇到与父母分享的内容相关的问题，但父母分享经历的权利与孩子的隐私权之间仍然存在紧张关系。

paragraphs.sourceText: E. “We’re in no way trying to silence parents’ voices,” Steinberg says. “At the same time, we recognize that children might have an interest in entering adulthood free to create their own digital footprint.” They cited a study presented earlier this year of 249 pairs of parents and their children in which twice as many children as parents wanted rules on what parents could share. “The parents said, ‘We don’t need rules—we’re fine,’ and the children said, ‘Our parents need rules,’” Keith says. “The children wanted autonomy about this issue and were worried about their parents sharing information about them.”
paragraphs.translationZh: E.“我们绝不试图压制父母的声音，”斯坦伯格说。 “与此同时，我们认识到，孩子们可能有兴趣进入成年后自由地创建自己的数字足迹。”他们引用了今年早些时候对 249 对父母及其孩子进行的一项研究，其中希望对父母可以分享的内容制定规则的孩子数量是父母的两倍。 “父母说，‘我们不需要规则——我们很好，’孩子们说，‘我们的父母需要规则，’”基思说。 “孩子们希望在这个问题上有自主权，并担心父母分享有关他们的信息。”

paragraphs.sourceText: F. Although the American Academy of Pediatrics offers guidelines recommending that parents model appropriate social media use for their children, it does not explicitly discuss oversharing by parents. “I think this is a very legitimate concern, and I appreciate their drawing our attention to it,” David Hill, a father of five, says. He sees a role for pediatricians to talk with parents about this, but believes the messaging must extend far beyond pediatricians’ offices. “I look forward to seeing researchers expand our understanding of the issue so we can translate it into effective education and policy,” he says.
paragraphs.translationZh: F. 尽管美国儿科学会提供了指导方针，建议父母为孩子树立适当的社交媒体使用榜样，但它没有明确讨论父母的过度分享。 “我认为这是一个非常合理的担忧，我感谢他们引起我们的关注，”五个孩子的父亲大卫·希尔说。他认为儿科医生可以与家长讨论这一问题，但他认为传递的信息必须远远超出儿科医生的办公室范围。 “我期待看到研究人员扩大我们对这个问题的理解，以便我们能够将其转化为有效的教育和政策，”他说。

paragraphs.sourceText: G. There’s been little research on the topic, Steinberg wrote in a law article about this issue. While states could pass laws related to sharing information about children online, Steinberg feels parents themselves are generally best suited to make these decisions for their families. “While we didn’t want to create any unnecessary panic, we did find some concerns that were troublesome, and we thought that parents or at least physicians should be aware of those potential risks,” Steinberg says. They include photos repurposed for inappropriate or illegal means, identity theft, embarrassment, bullying by peers or digital kidnapping.
paragraphs.translationZh: G. 关于这个话题的研究很少，斯坦伯格在一篇关于这个问题的法律文章中写道。虽然各州可以通过与在线共享儿童信息相关的法律，但斯坦伯格认为父母自己通常最适合为家人做出这些决定。 “虽然我们不想制造任何不必要的恐慌，但我们确实发现了一些麻烦的担忧，我们认为父母或至少医生应该意识到这些潜在的风险，”斯坦伯格说。其中包括以不适当或非法手段、身份盗窃、尴尬、同伴欺凌或数字绑架等方式重新利用的照片。

paragraphs.sourceText: H. But that’s the negative side, with risks that must be balanced against the benefits of sharing. Steinberg pointed out that parental sharing on social media helps build communities, connect spread-out families, provide support and raise awareness around important social issues for which parents might be their children’s only voice.
paragraphs.translationZh: H. 但这是消极的一面，必须平衡风险与共享的好处。斯坦伯格指出，父母在社交媒体上的分享有助于建立社区、联系分散的家庭、提供支持并提高对重要社会问题的认识，而父母可能是孩子唯一的声音。

paragraphs.sourceText: I. A C.S. Mott survey found among the 56 percent of mothers and 34 percent of fathers who discussed parenting on social media, 72 percent of them said sharing made them feel less alone, and nearly as many said sharing helped them worry less and gave them advice from other parents. The most common topics they discussed included kids’ sleep, nutrition, discipline, behavior problems and day care and preschool.
paragraphs.translationZh: I. C.S. Mott 的一项调查发现，56% 的母亲和 34% 的父亲在社交媒体上讨论育儿问题，其中 72% 的人表示分享让他们感觉不那么孤独，几乎同样多的人表示分享可以帮助他们减少担忧，并为他们提供其他父母的建议。他们讨论的最常见的话题包括孩子的睡眠、营养、纪律、行为问题以及日托和学前班。

paragraphs.sourceText: J. “There’s this peer-to-peer nature of health care these days with a profound opportunity for parents to learn helpful tips, safety and prevention efforts, pro-vaccine messages and all kinds of other messages from other parents in their social communities,” says Wendy Sue Swanson, a pediatrician and executive director of digital health at Seattle Children’s Hospital, where she blogs about her own parenting journey to help other parents. “They’re getting nurtured by people they’ve already selected that they trust,” she says.
paragraphs.translationZh: J. 西雅图儿童医院的儿科医生兼数字健康执行主任温迪·苏·斯旺森 (Wendy Sue Swanson) 表示：“如今，医疗保健具有这种点对点的性质，这为家长提供了一个绝佳的机会，让他们了解有用的提示、安全和预防工作、支持疫苗的信息以及来自其社交社区中其他家长的各种其他信息。”她在博客中讲述了自己帮助其他家长的育儿之旅。 “他们得到了他们已经选择并信任的人的培养，”她说。

paragraphs.sourceText: K. “How do we weigh the risks, how do we think about the benefits, and how do we alleviate the risks?” she says. “Those are the questions we need to ask ourselves, and everyone can have a different answer.”
paragraphs.translationZh: K.“我们如何权衡风险，如何考虑收益，以及如何减轻风险？”她说。 “这些都是我们需要问自己的问题，每个人都会有不同的答案。”

paragraphs.sourceText: L. Some parents find the best route for them is not to share at all. Bridget O’Hanlon and her husband, who live in Cleveland, decided before their daughter was born that they would not post her photos online. When a few family members did post pictures, O’Hanlon and her husband made their wishes clear. “It’s been hard not to share pictures of her because people always want to know how babies and toddlers (学走路的孩子) are doing and to see pictures, but we made the decision to have social media while she did not,” O’Hanlon said. Similarly, Alison Jamison of New York decided with her husband that their child had a right to their own online identity. They did use an invitation-only photo sharing platform so that friends and family, including those far away, could see the photos, but they stood firm, simply refusing to put their child’s photos on other social media platforms.
paragraphs.translationZh: L. 有些家长发现对他们来说最好的方法就是根本不分享。住在克利夫兰的布里奇特·奥汉隆和她的丈夫在女儿出生前就决定不会在网上发布她的照片。当一些家庭成员确实发布了照片时，奥汉隆和她的丈夫明确表达了他们的愿望。 “很难不分享她的照片，因为人们总是想知道婴儿和幼儿（学走路的孩子）在做什么并查看照片，但我们决定拥有社交媒体，而她却没有，”奥汉隆说。同样，纽约的艾莉森·贾米森 (Alison Jamison) 与她的丈夫决定，他们的孩子有权拥有自己的在线身份。他们确实使用了仅限邀请的照片共享平台，以便朋友和家人，包括远方的人，都可以看到这些照片，但他们立场坚定，只是拒绝将孩子的照片放在其他社交媒体平台上。

paragraphs.sourceText: M. “For most families, it’s a journey. Sometimes it goes wrong, but most of the time it doesn’t,” says Swanson, who recommends starting to ask children permission to post narratives or photos around ages 6 to 8. “We’ll learn more and more what our tolerance is. We can ask our kids to help us learn as a society what’s okay and what’s not.”
paragraphs.translationZh: M. 斯旺森说：“对于大多数家庭来说，这是一段旅程。有时会出错，但大多数时候不会出错。”他建议在 6 至 8 岁左右开始征求孩子们的许可，允许他们发布叙述或照片。“我们会越来越多地了解我们的容忍度是什么。我们可以要求我们的孩子帮助我们了解整个社会什么是可以的，什么是不可以的。”

paragraphs.sourceText: N. Indeed, that learning process goes both ways. Bria Dunham, a mother in Somerville, Massachusetts, was so excited to watch a moment of brotherly bonding while her first-grader and baby took a bath together that she snapped a few photos. But when she considered posting them online, she took the perspective of her son: How would he feel if his classmates’ parents saw photos of him chest-up in the bathtub? “It made me think about how I’m teaching him to have ownership of his own body and how what is shared today endures into the future,” Dunham says. “So I kept the pictures to myself and accepted this as one more step in supporting his increasing autonomy.”
paragraphs.translationZh: N. 事实上，学习过程是双向的。马萨诸塞州萨默维尔的一位母亲布里亚·邓纳姆 (Bria Dunham) 看到一年级学生和孩子一起洗澡时兄弟般的亲密时刻，她非常兴奋，拍了几张照片。但当她考虑将这些照片发布到网上时，她站在了儿子的角度：如果同学的父母看到他在浴缸里挺胸的照片，他会有什么感觉？ “这让我思考如何教导他拥有自己身体的所有权，以及今天分享的内容如何持续到未来，”邓纳姆说。 “所以我把这些照片留给了自己，并接受这是支持他日益增强的自主权的又一步。”

paragraphs.sourceText: 36. Steinberg argued parental sharing online can be beneficial.
paragraphs.translationZh: 36. 斯坦伯格认为，家长在线分享可能是有益的。

paragraphs.sourceText: 37. According to an expert, when children reach school age, they can help their parents learn what can and cannot be done.
paragraphs.translationZh: 37. 据专家称，当孩子达到学龄时，他们可以帮助父母了解什么可以做、什么不能做。

paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 46 to 50 are based on the following passage.
paragraphs.translationZh: 第 46 至 50 题基于以下段落。

paragraphs.sourceText: Perhaps it is time for farmers to put their feet up now that robots are used to inspect crops, dig up weeds, and even have become shepherds, too. Commercial growing fields are astronomically huge and take thousands of man-hours to operate. One prime example is one of Australia’s most isolated cattle stations, Suplejack Downs in the Northern Territory, extending across 4,000 square kilometers, taking over 13 hours to reach by car from the nearest major town—Alice Springs.
paragraphs.translationZh: 也许现在是农民们站起来的时候了，因为机器人被用来检查农作物、挖除杂草，甚至还成为了牧羊人。商业种植田规模巨大，需要数千工时才能运营。一个典型的例子是澳大利亚最偏僻的养牛场之一，位于北领地的 Suplejack Downs，占地 4,000 平方公里，从最近的主要城镇爱丽斯泉 (Alice Springs) 开车需要 13 个小时以上才能到达。

paragraphs.sourceText: The extreme isolation of these massive farms leaves them often unattended, and monitored only once or twice a year, which means if the livestock falls ill or requires assistance, it can be a long time for farmers to discover.
paragraphs.translationZh: 这些大型农场的极端隔离使得它们经常无人看管，每年只进行一到两次监测，这意味着如果牲畜生病或需要帮助，农民可能需要很长时间才能发现。

paragraphs.sourceText: However, robots are coming to the rescue. Robots are currently under a two-year trial in Wales which will train “farmbots” to herd, monitor the health of livestock, and make sure there is enough pasture for them to graze on. The robots are equipped with many sensors to identify conditions of the environment, cattle and food, using thermal and vision sensors that detect changes in body temperature.
paragraphs.translationZh: 然而，机器人正在前来救援。机器人目前正在威尔士进行为期两年的试验，该试验将训练“农场机器人”放牧、监测牲畜的健康状况，并确保有足够的牧场供它们吃草。这些机器人配备了许多传感器来识别环境、牛和食物的状况，使用热传感器和视觉传感器来检测体温的变化。

paragraphs.sourceText: “You’ve also got color, texture and shape sensors looking down at the ground to check pasture quality,” says Salah Sukkarieh of the University of Sydney, who will carry out trials on several farms in central New South Wales.
paragraphs.translationZh: 悉尼大学的 Salah Sukkarieh 表示：“颜色、质地和形状传感器可以俯视地面，以检查牧场质量。”他将在新南威尔士州中部的几个农场进行试验。

paragraphs.sourceText: During the trials, the robot algorithms (算法) and mechanics will be fine-tuned to make it better suited to ailing livestock and ensure it safely navigates around potential hazards including trees, mud, swamps, and hills.
paragraphs.translationZh: 在试验期间，机器人的算法和机制将进行微调，使其更适合生病的牲畜，并确保其安全地绕过树木、泥土、沼泽和山丘等潜在危险。

paragraphs.sourceText: “We want to improve the quality of animal health and make it easier for farmers to maintain large landscapes where animals roam free,” says Sukkarieh.
paragraphs.translationZh: “我们希望提高动物健康质量，让农民更容易维护动物自由漫步的大片景观，”Sukkarieh 说。

paragraphs.sourceText: The robots are not limited to herding and monitoring livestock. They have been created to count individual fruit, inspect crops, and even pull weeds.
paragraphs.translationZh: 这些机器人不仅限于放牧和监控牲畜。它们的用途是计算单个水果的数量、检查农作物，甚至拔除杂草。

paragraphs.sourceText: Many robots are equipped with high-tech sensors and complex learning algorithms to avoid injuring humans as they work side by side. The robots also learn the most efficient and safest passages, and allow engineers and farmers to analyze and better optimize the attributes and tasks of the robot, as well as provide a live stream giving real-time feedback on exactly what is happening on the farms.
paragraphs.translationZh: 许多机器人都配备了高科技传感器和复杂的学习算法，以避免在并肩工作时伤害人类。机器人还可以学习最高效、最安全的通道，让工程师和农民能够分析和更好地优化机器人的属性和任务，并提供直播，实时反馈农场发生的情况。

paragraphs.sourceText: Of course, some worry lies in replacing agricultural workers. However, it is farmers that are pushing for the advancements due to ever-increasing labor vacancies, making it difficult to maintain large-scale operations.
paragraphs.translationZh: 当然，一些担忧在于替代农业工人。然而，由于劳动力空缺不断增加，大规模经营难以维持，推动进步的是农民。

paragraphs.sourceText: The robots have provided major benefits to farmers in various ways, from hunting and pulling weeds to monitoring the condition of every single fruit. Future farms will likely experience a greater deal of autonomy as robots take up more and more farm work efficiently.
paragraphs.translationZh: 这些机器人以各种方式为农民带来了巨大的好处，从打猎、除草到监测每种水果的状况。随着机器人有效地承担越来越多的农场工作，未来的农场可能会获得更大的自主权。

paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 51 to 55 are based on the following passage
paragraphs.translationZh: 第 51 至 55 题基于以下段落

paragraphs.sourceText: The public must be able to understand the basics of science to make informed decisions. Perhaps the most dramatic example of the negative consequences of poor communication between scientists and the public is the issue of climate change, where a variety of factors, not the least of which is a breakdown in the transmission of fundamental climate data to the general public, has contributed to widespread mistrust and misunderstanding of scientists and their research.
paragraphs.translationZh: 公众必须能够了解科学基础知识才能做出明智的决定。也许科学家和公众之间沟通不畅所造成的负面后果的最引人注目的例子是气候变化问题，其中多种因素，尤其是向公众传输基本气候数据的中断，导致了对科学家及其研究的普遍不信任和误解。

paragraphs.sourceText: The issue of climate change also illustrates how the public acceptance and understanding of science (or the lack of it) can influence governmental decision-making with regard to regulation, science policy and research funding.
paragraphs.translationZh: 气候变化问题还说明了公众对科学的接受和理解（或缺乏科学）如何影响政府在监管、科学政策和研究经费方面的决策。

paragraphs.sourceText: However, the importance of effective communication with a general audience is not limited to hot issues like climate change. It is also critical for socially charged neuroscience issues such as the genetic basis for a particular behavior, the therapeutic potential of stem cell therapy for neurodegenerative diseases, or the use of animal models, areas where the public understanding of science can also influence policy and funding decisions. Furthermore, with continuing advances in individual genome (基因组) sequencing and the advent of personalized medicine, more non-scientists will need to be comfortable analyzing complex scientific information to make decisions that directly affect their quality of life.
paragraphs.translationZh: 然而，与普通受众进行有效沟通的重要性不仅限于气候变化等热点问题。它对于社会性的神经科学问题也至关重要，例如特定行为的遗传基础、干细胞疗法对神经退行性疾病的治疗潜力或动物模型的使用，在这些领域，公众对科学的理解也可以影响政策和资助决策。此外，随着个体基因组（基因组）测序的不断进步和个性化医疗的出现，更多的非科学家将需要轻松地分析复杂的科学信息，以做出直接影响他们生活质量的决策。

paragraphs.sourceText: Science journalism is the main channel for the popularization of scientific information among the public. Much has been written about how the relationship between scientists and the media can shape the efficient transmission of scientific advances to the public. Good science journalists are specialists in making complex topics accessible to a general audience, while adhering to scientific accuracy.
paragraphs.translationZh: 科学新闻是向公众普及科学信息的主渠道。关于科学家和媒体之间的关系如何影响向公众有效传播科学进步的文章已经有很多。优秀的科学记者是让普通受众了解复杂话题的专家，同时坚持科学的准确性。

paragraphs.sourceText: Unfortunately, pieces of science journalism can also oversimplify and generalize their subject material to the point that the basic information conveyed is obscured or at worst, obviously wrong. The impact of a basic discovery on human health can be exaggerated so that the public thinks a miraculous cure is a few months to years away when in reality the significance of the study is far more limited.
paragraphs.translationZh: 不幸的是，科学新闻也可能过度简化和概括其主题材料，以至于所传达的基本信息变得模糊，或者在最坏的情况下，明显是错误的。一项基本发现对人类健康的影响可能会被夸大，以至于公众认为奇迹般的治愈方法还需要几个月到几年的时间，而实际上这项研究的意义要有限得多。

paragraphs.sourceText: Even though scientists play a part in transmitting information to journalists and ultimately the public, too often the blame for ineffective communication is placed on the side of the journalists. We believe that at least part of the problem lies in places other than the interaction between scientists and members of the media, and exists because for one thing we underestimate how difficult it is for scientists to communicate effectively with a diversity of audiences, and for another most scientists do not receive formal training in science communication.
paragraphs.translationZh: 尽管科学家在向记者以及最终向公众传递信息方面发挥着重要作用，但沟通无效的责任往往归咎于记者。我们认为，至少部分问题存在于科学家与媒体成员之间互动以外的地方，之所以存在，是因为一方面我们低估了科学家与不同受众进行有效沟通的难度，另一方面大多数科学家没有接受过科学传播方面的正式培训。
